nodes.name: Hydrothermal synthesis of NiMoO4·xH2O/NF
nodes.procedure: Dissolve 2 mmol (0.5815 g) of nickel nitrate (Ni(NO3)2·6H2O) and 3 mmol (0.4839 g) of ammonium molybdate ((NH4)6Mo7O24·4H2O) in 30 mL of deionized water and stir thoroughly until a homogeneous solution is formed. The obtained mixture and the pretreated NF were placed into an autoclave with a total volume of 50 mL. The hydrothermal reaction is carried out at 150°C for 6 h. Once the reaction is complete, allow the system to cool naturally to room temperature before removing the sample. Subsequently, the product was washed with deionized water to remove surface unstable substances and then dried in an oven at 60°C for 10 h.

nodes.name: Solvothermal anchoring of Ru nanoparticles
nodes.procedure: Forty milligram of ruthenium trichloride (RuCl3) was dissolved in 20 mL of anhydrous ethanol. Subsequently, a self-supporting Fe-NiMoO4 was immersed in the solution before transferring the mixture to a 50 mL autoclave. The system was subjected to a solvothermal reaction at 90°C for 6 h. Once cooled to room temperature after the reaction, the final sample was retrieved. It was thoroughly washed with deionized water and then dried overnight in a drying oven at 60°C. For comparative purposes, a Ru/NiMoO4 catalyst was synthesized under identical experimental conditions using NiMoO4·xH2O as the precursor.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows hollow nanorods of Ru/Fe-NiMoO₄ with enhanced surface roughness and suppressed Ru particle agglomeration.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As illustrated in Figure 1b and Figure S3, the solvent thermal treatment further enhanced the surface roughness of the Ru/Fe-NiMoO₄ nanorods while preserving their hollow structural characteristics.

properties.description: High-magnification SEM image of nanostructured material

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM reveals Ru nanoparticles highly dispersed on hollow nanorods of Ru/Fe-NiMoO₄ with diameter ~200 nm and nanocavities ~27 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: TEM and HAADF-STEM images reveal that Ru nanoparticles are highly dispersed on the hollow nanorods of Ru/Fe-NiMoO₄ which enhances the utilization efficiency of the Ru species in catalytic reactions (Figure 1c,d; Figure S6).

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM shows uniform elemental distribution of Ni, Mo, O, Fe, and Ru across Ru/Fe-NiMoO₄ nanorods.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Moreover, HAADF-STEM results of Ru/Fe-NiMoO₄ reveal a uniform distribution of Ni, Mo, O, Fe, and Ru elements across the nanorods (Figure 1h,l).

properties.description: Composite TEM/STEM image with scale bar

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows lattice spacing of 0.274 nm for NiMoO₄ (Region I), amorphous surface (Region II), and 0.206 nm for Ru(101) plane (Region III) with low crystallinity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The measured lattice stripe spacing of 0.206 nm is associated with the (101) crystal plane of Ru (Figure 1g).

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-OES confirms Ru content of 2.03 wt.% in Ru/Fe-NiMoO₄.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Inductively coupled plasma emission spectroscopy (ICP-OES) analysis confirmed that the Ru content is as low as 2.03 wt.% (Table S2).

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD shows characteristic peaks of NiMoO₄·xH₂O and NiMoO₄; no detectable Ru peaks due to low crystallinity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Notably, the XRD pattern of Ru/Fe-NiMoO₄ does not exhibit any detectable Ru diffraction peaks, which is consistent with the HRTEM observations of low-crystallinity Ru particles.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows Ni 2p peaks at 856.98 eV and 874.64 eV (Ni²⁺, shifted +0.70 eV vs Fe-NiMoO₄), Mo 3d at 232.54/235.69 eV (Mo⁶⁺, shifted +0.46 eV), Fe 2p with Fe²⁺ (708.60/721.27 eV) and Fe³⁺ (712.24/723.97 eV, shifted +0.38 eV), Ru 3p with Ru⁰ (462.48/484.68 eV) and Ruⁿ⁺ (465.78/487.58 eV), increased unsaturated oxygen content.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution XPS spectrum of Ni 2p further shows characteristic peaks at 856.98 and 874.64 eV... the Ru 3p region, the peaks at 462.48 and 484.68 eV can be assigned to metallic Ru 3p₃/₂ and Ru 3p₁/₂ of Ru⁰, respectively...

nodes.characterization_summary: EPR signals at g=2.003 confirm oxygen vacancies, with intensity: Ru/Fe-NiMoO₄ > Fe-NiMoO₄ > NiMoO₄·xH₂O.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The EPR signals of Ru/Fe-NiMoO₄, Fe-NiMoO₄, and NiMoO₄·xH₂O are all located at g = 2.003, a characteristic signal for oxygen vacancies (Figure S8d).

nodes.characterization_summary: Fe K-edge XANES: oxidation state between +2/+3; FT-EXAFS: Fe-O at 1.50 Å (CN=5.11, bond length 1.92 Å), no Fe-Fe coordination; Ru K-edge XANES: valence between 0/+4, shifted to lower energy; FT-EXAFS: Ru-Ru at 2.40 Å (CN=2.59, bond length 2.67 Å).
nodes.evidence_snippet: As illustrated in Figure 2d, the Fe K-edge Xray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) spectrum reveals that the absorption edge of Ru/Fe-NiMoO₄ is positioned between that of FeO and Fe₂O₃... R space and k space FT-EXAFS analysis of Ru/Fe-NiMoO₄ revealed a Ru-Ru coordination number of 2.59 and bond distance of 2.67 Å.

nodes.characterization_summary: UPS shows work function 3.71 eV for Ru/Fe-NiMoO₄ (vs 4.17 eV for Ru/NiMoO₄) and valence band top at 2.90 eV.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Φ values of Ru/NiMoO₄ and Ru/Fe-NiMoO₄ were calculated to be 4.17 and 3.71 eV, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: CV in non-Faradaic region gives double-layer capacitance C_dl = 110.20 mF/cm² corresponding to ECSA = 1503.83 cm² for Ru/Fe-NiMoO₄.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the C_dl value for Ru/Fe-NiMoO₄ was calculated to be 110.20 mFcm⁻²... Correspondingly, Ru/Fe-NiMoO₄ exhibited the highest ECSA value (1503.83 cm²).

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman shows deconvoluted O-H peaks at 3225 cm⁻¹ (tetrahedral), 3450 cm⁻¹ (octahedral), 3615 cm⁻¹ (dangling); faster decrease of ν3 peak ratio indicates enhanced water dissociation by Ru.
nodes.evidence_snippet: both Ru/Fe-NiMoO₄ and Fe-NiMoO₄ display a broad peak at approximately 3500 cm⁻¹, which can be further deconvoluted into three peaks at (ν1)3225 cm⁻¹, (ν2)3450 cm⁻¹, and (ν3)3615 cm⁻¹.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ ATR-FTIR shows HzOR intermediates: NH₂ stretch ~3358 cm⁻¹, NH₂ twist ~1615 cm⁻¹, N-N stretch ~1098 cm⁻¹ with higher concentrations on Ru/Fe-NiMoO₄.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The peak intensities of the N₂Hₙ (1≤n≤4) intermediates involved in the HzOR increase with increasing working potential. These peaks include the NH₂ stretching mode at approximately 3358 cm⁻¹, the NH₂ twisting mode at around 1615 cm⁻¹, and the N-N stretching mode at approximately 1098 cm⁻¹.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS confirms homogeneous distribution of Ni, Mo, O, Fe in Fe-NiMoO₄.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure S5c-f present high-angle annular dark-field scanning TEM (HAADF-STEM) and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) results for Fe-NiMoO₄, demonstrating a homogeneous distribution of Ni, Mo, O, and Fe elements.
